subject: chemistry
title: Group 0: Noble Gases
welcome_lead: Stable, sparkling and seriously unreactive: the noble family of gases.
meta_desc: Meet the noble gases in this KS3 chemistry adventure on group 0 of the periodic table.
final_note: You can now explain why noble gases are so chemically chilled.

concepts.def: Noble gases: helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, radon.
Very unreactive gas with a full outer electron shell.
Lighter than air; used to fill balloons.
Used in some light bulbs to stop the filament burning.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Group 0 (sometimes Group 8) sits on the far right of the table. The noble gases are all colourless gases at room temperature.

Helium, neon, argon and friends.

Noble gases have a full outer electron shell. They don't need to gain, lose or share electrons, so they hardly ever react.

They are stable just as they are.

Because they don't react, noble gases are very useful:

Helium fills airships and balloons; neon glows in signs; argon protects metal welding and light bulb filaments.

options: They have a full outer electron shell
They are too heavy
They are too cold
They are not real gases

options: Argon
Helium
Neon

mcqs.q: At which electrode are positive ions reduced during electrolysis?
options: Positive ions are reduced at the anode because that's where positive things go.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
At the cathode (the negative electrode) — positive ions gain electrons there.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.
Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
